title: Four ways to adjust an option selling program in a volatile market
summary: If covered calls or cash-secured puts have hurt you lately, the speaker lists four changes: sell monthlies instead of weeklies to cut gamma and smooth P&L, move strikes further out of the money, trade smaller, and avoid a position that can lose a multiple of the premium in one day when the stock bounces hard.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $100 in a volatile market, with implied volatility near 45%.
A weekly put close to the money has high gamma: its P&L swings hard with each move in the stock.
A monthly put further out of the money has less gamma, so its P&L curve is smoother.
The difference shows the gamma you remove by going further out in time and wider on the strike.
The wider strike also moves the breakeven down, so the stock has more room to fall.
Fewer contracts shrink both curves. Size so one bad day does not cost a multiple of the premium.

takeaways: Selling monthlies instead of weeklies reduces gamma and smooths the P&L.
Strikes further out of the money give the stock more room before you lose.
Smaller size limits the damage from a sharp move against the position.
A short option can lose a multiple of its premium in one day if the stock jumps.
caveats: The fourth item is partly garbled in the transcript. Strikes and volatility in the chart are example values.
